Design system · main

NanoClaw design system

One brand colour, mint, on neutrals tinted with its hue. Mint means “go, active, NanoClaw, done”; amber and red only ever mean warning and error. Personality comes from the mascot and the chunky wordmark, not from more colours. Type is Inter, as on nanoclaw.dev and the docs. Dark is the default theme.

1brand colour: mint #56EDD6. No second accent.
≤ 10%of any screen is mint. Scarcity is what makes it point.
1primary (mint) button per view.
44/44colour pairs pass WCAG AA in both themes (table below).

01

Principles

Four decisions everything else follows from. Lavender and coral were tried as second accents and dropped: coral read as an error, lavender looked arbitrary.

Colour carries meaning, not decoration

Mint = primary action, active, brand, success. Amber = warning. Red = error. Tips and notes stay neutral, with an icon. If a colour doesn’t mean one of those, it’s a neutral.

Neutrals are tinted, never navy

Every grey carries a trace of mint’s hue so the palette feels like one family. The background is a near-black (#0C1213), not navy: the mascot’s navy outline would vanish on navy.

Borders over shadows

On dark, shadows barely show. Depth is a step up in surface plus a 1px border. A shadow is kept for things that float: menus, dialogs, toasts.

Character from the mascot and wordmark

The waving shrimp and the heavy rounded wordmark are the personality. The UI around them stays calm, so they stand out.

02

Colour

Ramps built in OKLCH at mint’s hue (181°), so steps are even in perceived lightness. Brand values are pinned: mint-400 is the brand mint, mint-700 is mint for text on light. Click any swatch or value to copy it.

Mint

Neutral (tinted)

Status

Success has no colour of its own: it is mint, with a check icon.

Logo colours. Dark: white “Nano” + mint #56EDD6 “Claw”, mascot with the pale #D6FCF7 rim. Light: the whole wordmark in navy #080037, the mascot’s own outline colour, no rim. Mint-700 #0B7566 is for UI text on light, never the wordmark.

One mint. Mint-400 #56EDD6 is the mascot’s fill, the wordmark’s “Claw” and the UI mint: one value everywhere. The mascot’s shading tones (shadow #44BBAC, light #89EDD6) belong to the artwork only, never to UI.

One near-black. #0C1213 (neutral-950, the dark --nc-bg) is the brand near-black: pages, dark merch, the reversed and mint variants. The one exception is a preview of the README logos as GitHub shows them, which uses GitHub’s own dark background, #0d1117.

Contrast checks

Every text and control pair in the system, measured with the WCAG 2 formula. 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for control outlines and the focus ring. Mint #56EDD6 on the light background is only 1.38:1, so on light it is a fill (with a dark label and a mint-700 edge), never text.

03

Logo

The lockup is the mascot to the left of the wordmark. The mascot is a shrimp with a waving claw: mint fill, soft shading, a thick navy outline. On dark: “Nano” in white, “Claw” in mint #56EDD6, and a thin pale rim, #D6FCF7, around the mascot so its navy outline and antennae don’t sink into the background. On light: the whole wordmark in navy #080037, the mascot’s own outline colour, and no rim (a darker teal “Claw” never quite matched the mascot’s mint).

On dark · white + mint wordmark, pale rim
On light · all-navy wordmark, no rim

Proportions, clear space and minimum sizes

½h ½h

h = mascot height. The wordmark’s cap height is 40% of h, centred on the mascot’s body (antennae left out), with a gap of 0.6 × the cap height (about 0.24h).
Keep clear space of ½h on every side.

  • Below 48px the full mascot turns to noise: use the app icon (next section).
  • Print: lockup at least 25mm wide.
  • Wordmark alone works from 80px wide (social headers, footers).
  • Files: avatar/logo/bigger-wordmark/nanoclaw-logo-dark-40 and …-light-40 (SVG and PNG, transparent; the README pair avatar/logo/nanoclaw-logo-{dark,light} is the same artwork): dark = white “Nano” + mint “Claw” with the pale rim; light = all-navy #080037 wordmark, no rim. The page and the files use the same colours.

Wordmark only, for small sizes

Below 32px tall the mascot is too small to read (under about 24px), so drop it and use the wordmark alone, in the same colours: all navy on light; white “Nano” and mint “Claw” on dark, with no rim (the rim belongs to the mascot).

On dark · 160, 96 and 64px wide
On light · 160, 96 and 64px wide

  • Clear space: the wordmark’s cap height (about its full height, as it has no descenders) on every side.
  • Minimum size: 64px wide on screen (about 9px tall). At 56px it still reads; at 48px the counters of the “a” and “o” fill in.
  • Files: avatar/logo/wordmark/nanoclaw-wordmark-{light,dark}, plus one-colour navy, black, white and mint: SVG, PDF and PNG (512 and 2048 wide), transparent, tight to the ink.

Do and don’t

Favicon and app icon

One icon for every small square: the mascot’s bust, cropped to fill a pale #D6FCF7 rounded tile (corner radius 22%). It is the same production vector at every size, unhinted, so it stays the mascot rather than a redrawing. The pale tile reads on both dark and light tabs.

05

Logo variants

The same production vectors, for media that can’t print the full-colour mark. Each variant comes for the mascot, the 40% lockup and the app icon, as SVG, PDF and PNG (512 and 2048).

Full colour by default; monochrome only when the medium allows one ink. The full-colour mascot is never recoloured: a one-colour job uses the one-colour artwork, not a tinted copy of the colour file.

When to use which

VariantInksUse whenFolder
Full colourFull colour, shadedThe default, everywhere it can be: screens, digital print, stickers.Logo and App icon sections
FlatNavy, mint, white shineEmbroidery, screen print, vinyl, small sizes: no shadow or light tones.flat/
Two-colour spotNavy + mint, no tintsTwo-ink print: the shine prints in mint, the wordmark in navy.two-colour-spot/
One colour, navy1 ink: #080037One ink on a light ground: stamps, letterpress, single-colour merch.one-colour-navy/
One colour, black1 ink: #000000Black-only print: forms, receipts, fax, laser printers.one-colour-black/
One colour, reversed1 ink: whiteWhite ink on a dark ground: dark tees, foil, white vinyl on glass.one-colour-reversed/
One colour, mint1 ink: #56EDD6Mint ink on near-black: dark merch, glow-style signage.one-colour-mint/
GreyscaleLuminance-matched greysNewspaper, mono print and photocopies, where colour isn’t available but tones are.greyscale/
OutlineNavy lines, white fillLaser engraving, colouring pages, line-art merch.outline/

How the one-colour versions are built

  • Positive (navy, black): the ink is the mascot’s own linework; the mint is knocked out, so the paper becomes the body. Light body, dark lines, as in the colour mark.
  • Reversed (white, mint): a solid body on near-black #0C1213. The ink is the mascot’s colour fills and an outer rim; the mascot’s own linework (outline, inner lines, antennae, eyes, mouth) becomes a dark gap between them, so every line still shows and the eye shines stay ink. The rim is offset from the silhouette by the outline’s width, like the dark-mode rim.
  • App icon: the positive icon is the linework inside a tile keyline as thick as the mascot’s outline; the reversed icon is a solid tile with the linework knocked out.
  • Greyscale maps each colour to the grey of the same luminance, so contrast stays where it was.

Files: avatar/variants/<variant>/, with a README and a contact sheet (variants-sheet.png). The wordmark alone comes in the same one-colour inks (navy, black, white, mint) in avatar/logo/wordmark/.

06

Typography

NanoClaw is set in Inter, headings and body, with JetBrains Mono for code. That’s what nanoclaw.dev and docs.nanoclaw.dev use today, so the system follows them. Both fonts are free under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 and are embedded in this page.

Headings and body
Inter

By Rasmus Andersson. Variable: weights 100–900, optical size 14–32. Headings use ExtraBold 800 (display), Bold 700 (H1, H2) and SemiBold 600 (H3, H4) with tight tracking. Body text uses 400, UI labels 500 and emphasis 600. Has tabular figures (tnum). Fallback: system-ui.

Code
JetBrains Mono

By JetBrains. Tall x-height and clear 0O 1lI, made for terminals. 400 for code, 500 for emphasis. Fallback: ui-monospace, SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas.

07

Voice and tone

NanoClaw sounds like a friend who runs a home server. They know how it works, they’ll tell you when they don’t know, and they’re glad you asked. When setup succeeds, “Your agent’s up. Say hi. 👋” is plenty. When setup fails, tell the reader what happened and help them take the next step.

Make it easy to follow

Use everyday words and short sentences. Assume the reader is capable and may be seeing NanoClaw for the first time. When a technical term matters, use it and explain it where it first appears. Readers who learn the word container here will recognize it when they open Docker.

  • Make ownership concrete. Say “your agent,” “your machine,” or “your fork” when it helps someone understand what they control. Be just as clear about what goes elsewhere. “If you use a hosted model, its provider receives the content your agent sends in a request.”
  • Explain how it works. “The credential gateway adds the API key when it forwards the request” tells the reader something they can use. A claim like “bank-grade security” leaves them guessing.
  • Give the next useful action. An error message should say what failed. If the cause is uncertain, give the reader a way to check it. Save the fix for when you know what needs fixing.
  • Use numbers you can verify. Check timings, version numbers, and contributor counts against the code, measurement, or release you’re describing.
  • Link where the detail lives. Keep the install command in Quick Start. Link to the installation guide for what the wizard does at each step. Give the link a name that tells readers what they’ll find.

Match the moment

Where you’re writing How NanoClaw sounds
README, website, onboarding Warm and direct. Show what someone can do with their agent and give them a place to start.
Guides, reference docs, CLI help Practical and precise. Use the names people see on screen. Give an example they can try.
Errors, warnings, privacy, security Calm and literal. Explain what happened or what will happen, who or what it affects, and what the reader can do.
Release notes Specific and appreciative. Name a change someone will notice. Credit the people who made it happen.
Social, Discord, stickers, merch Conversational and playful. There’s room for a shrimp joke if you have a good one.

The subject takes priority over the channel. A security advisory deserves the same care in Discord as it does in SECURITY.md.

Write steps people can follow

For installation, migration, troubleshooting, credential rotation, backup, restore, and uninstall procedures, draw on ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Give each step one action. Put a condition before the action it affects. Use the same name for the same thing throughout. When the result might surprise a new user, explain what success looks like. These are principles we borrow from the standard. ASD-STE100, Issue 9

For example, a macOS troubleshooting entry could read:

Setup can’t reach Docker

  1. Open Docker Desktop.
  2. When Docker Desktop reports that the engine is running, run docker ps.
  3. If the command prints a list of containers, run bash nanoclaw.sh again.

An empty list is fine. It means Docker answered and no containers are running.

Leave room for personality

Take the reader’s time seriously. Take yourself a little less seriously. Our mascot is a shrimp waving a claw. A dry aside, a cheerful emoji, or a small moment of delight can make the product feel welcoming. Routine instructions can be routine. “Install Docker” is a perfectly good heading.

Moment Example
First successful run “Your agent’s up. Say hi. 👋”
Empty schedule “Nothing scheduled. Your agent has the afternoon free.”
An optional integration “Want to talk to your agent in Telegram? Run /add-telegram in your checkout.”
A release announcement “Each agent can now have its own Slack app, so you can see who replied.”

Let humor land on us or the situation. When the reader is stuck, the most considerate thing we can offer is a clear next step. Avoid jokes at someone’s expense, including people who use or build other projects.

The mascot and emoji

The mascot can speak in short first-person lines on stickers, social posts, or a playful 404 page. In setup and chat, make it clear who’s speaking. Readers should be able to tell your agent’s reply from an installer message.

Emoji are welcome. Use them to help someone find a section, recognize a status, or enjoy a moment. A 🚀 beside Quick Start, a 👋 after a successful setup, and a 🦐 in a release announcement all feel at home. Use your judgment about frequency. When the meaning matters, put it in words too: “⚠️ This removes the agent’s files.”

Names and mechanics

Write NanoClaw for the open-source project and NanoCo for the company. Preserve literal casing in commands, paths, repository names, and URLs. Use US English and the official spelling of names such as Claude Code, WhatsApp, and iMessage.

Follow the website’s Title Case convention for navigation, buttons, and section titles. Use sentence case in body copy. Format commands, skills, environment variables, and paths as code. Leave the $ prompt out of copyable commands so readers can paste them directly into a terminal.

Before publishing

Read it aloud. Would you say it this way to someone you were helping? Check the facts, make sure the reader knows who’s speaking, and see whether they can tell what to do next.

radius-xs4px · kbd, tags

Pills for buttons and badges; 8–10px for everything boxy. Nested corners: inner = outer − padding.

Borders and elevation

Level 0 · bgThe page. No border.
Level 1 · surface + borderCards, callouts, code, inputs, banner.
Level 2 · surface-2 + border + shadowOnly for floating layers: menus, dialogs, toasts.

Focus ring

2px solid --nc-focus, 2px offset, on every interactive element, keyboard only (:focus-visible). Never removed.

Focused link

Iconography

  • Lucide (open source, also Mintlify’s lucide library): rounded caps match the wordmark.
  • 2px stroke at 16–24px; currentColor.
  • Icons are muted; mint only when active or interactive.
  • Status icons always sit with a label.

Motion

  • 120ms hover and press; 200ms small enters; 320ms panels.
  • Ease cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1); exits a little faster.
  • The mascot waves once, on first view of a hero or an empty state. Never loops.
  • prefers-reduced-motion sets durations to 0.

09

Components

Each one live in both themes, built only from the semantic tokens. Hover them; tab through them to see focus.

Buttons

Primary is the mint pill: one per view. On light it gets a mint-700 edge, since the mint fill alone is 1.38:1 against the page. Secondary is neutral with an outline; ghost for low-emphasis actions; destructive is red with an icon, and asks to confirm.

Links

Mint text (mint-700 on light). Underlined in body copy so colour isn’t the only cue; a standalone call to action can drop it and add an arrow.

Get a Claude API key before you start. Links are mint text, underlined on hover and always underlined inside long prose.

10

Usage rules

Mint ≤ about 10% of a screen

Logo, one primary button, the active nav item, links and checks. If a screen looks minty, something that should be neutral isn’t.

One primary button per view

Everything else is secondary or ghost. Two mint buttons means no button is primary.

Never colour alone

Every status has an icon and words: a check for success, a triangle for warning, a cross for error. Active nav is tint + weight; links are underlined in prose; invalid fields have a message.

Colour-blind check

Mint, amber and red differ in lightness as well as hue, but with red–green colour blindness mint and amber can look alike. The icon-and-label rule covers it; check new screens with a deuteranopia and protanopia simulation (Chrome DevTools → Rendering → Emulate vision deficiencies).

Status colours stay in their lane

Amber and red are never decoration, illustration or a “fun” highlight. If it isn’t a warning or an error, it isn’t amber or red.

Light theme

Mint #56EDD6 becomes a fill only: buttons (dark label + mint-700 edge), the mascot, tints. Mint text, links, underlines and outlines are mint-700 #0B7566. The logo’s wordmark is all navy #080037 on light; only on dark is “Claw” mint.

/* Semantic tokens: light */

:root {
  /* Type */
  --nc-font-heading: "Inter", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
  --nc-font-body: "Inter", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
  --nc-font-mono: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
  /* Spacing (4px base) */
  --nc-space-0-5: 2px; --nc-space-1: 4px; --nc-space-2: 8px; --nc-space-3: 12px;
  --nc-space-4: 16px; --nc-space-5: 20px; --nc-space-6: 24px; --nc-space-8: 32px;
  --nc-space-10: 40px; --nc-space-12: 48px; --nc-space-16: 64px; --nc-space-24: 96px;
  /* Radii */
  --nc-radius-xs: 4px; --nc-radius-sm: 6px; --nc-radius-md: 8px;
  --nc-radius-lg: 10px; --nc-radius-xl: 16px; --nc-radius-pill: 999px;
  /* Elevation: borders first; a shadow only for overlays */
  --nc-shadow-overlay: 0 12px 32px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45);
  /* Focus */
  --nc-focus-ring: 0 0 0 2px var(--nc-bg), 0 0 0 4px var(--nc-focus);
  /* Motion */
  --nc-duration-fast: 120ms; --nc-duration-base: 200ms; --nc-duration-slow: 320ms;
  --nc-ease-standard: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);
  --nc-ease-exit: cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 1, 1);
}
[data-theme="light"] { --nc-shadow-overlay: 0 1px 2px rgb(12 18 19 / 0.06), 0 8px 24px rgb(12 18 19 / 0.10); }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  :root { --nc-duration-fast: 0ms; --nc-duration-base: 0ms; --nc-duration-slow: 0ms; }
}

Mintlify (docs.nanoclaw.dev)

Colour roles, from Mintlify’s schema reference

  • primary: “emphasis in light mode” → #0B7566 (mint-700, 5.3:1).
  • light: “emphasis in dark mode” → #56EDD6 (13:1).
  • dark: “buttons and hover states across both modes”, with white text → #0B7566: white on it is 5.6:1 (#0E816F would also pass at 4.79).

What changes from today

  • Teal #2DD4BF / #5EEAD4 / #14B8A6 → the mint above. White on today’s #14B8A6 is about 2.5:1, so banner and button text fail now.
  • Background set to the tinted near-black and light bg.
  • appearance stays dark + strict.
  • fonts stay as they are: Inter 600 for headings, Inter 400 for body.
  • The banner is restyled to a neutral strip in style.css.

style.css for Mintlify
/* style.css in the docs repo. Mintlify loads any .css file in the content folder.
   Selectors are from Mintlify's documented hooks (#banner, .callout, #sidebar-content li[data-active]).
   Mintlify toggles dark mode with a "dark" class on <html>; check both in DevTools before shipping. */
:root {
  --nc-bg: #0C1213; --nc-surface: #131B1D; --nc-surface-2: #1A2426; --nc-border: #263234;
  --nc-text: #EAF4F2; --nc-text-muted: #93A9A6;
  --nc-accent: #56EDD6; --nc-accent-tint: #12302C; --nc-on-accent: #0C1213;
  --nc-warning: #F5B84B; --nc-warning-tint: #2A2214;
  --nc-danger: #FF6B6B; --nc-danger-tint: #2C1617;
}

/* Banner: a neutral strip with a mint link, not a coloured block.
   (Mintlify paints it with colors.dark and white text by default.) */
#banner {
  background: var(--nc-surface) !important;
  color: var(--nc-text-muted) !important;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--nc-border);
}
#banner a { color: var(--nc-accent) !important; text-decoration: none; font-weight: 500; }
#banner a:hover { text-decoration: underline; }

/* Primary buttons in dark mode: mint fill, dark label (13:1).
   colors.dark (#0B7566, white label 5.6:1) stays for hover states and light mode. */
html.dark #topbar-cta-button a,
html.dark [data-component-name="primary-header-button"] {
  background: var(--nc-accent) !important;
  color: var(--nc-on-accent) !important;
  border-radius: 999px;
}

/* Active sidebar item: mint tint + mint label, no left bar. */
#sidebar-content li[data-active] a {
  background: var(--nc-accent-tint);
  color: var(--nc-accent);
  border-radius: 8px;
}

/* Callouts: 10px radius, neutral by default (Tip / Note / Info).
   Warning and error get their tints; find the attribute or class Mintlify puts on each
   callout type in DevTools and fill it in below (shown here as data-callout-type). */
.callout { border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid var(--nc-border); background: var(--nc-surface); }
.callout[data-callout-type="warning"] { background: var(--nc-warning-tint); border-color: transparent; }
.callout[data-callout-type="warning"] svg { color: var(--nc-warning); }
.callout[data-callout-type="danger"] { background: var(--nc-danger-tint); border-color: transparent; }
.callout[data-callout-type="danger"] svg { color: var(--nc-danger); }
.callout[data-callout-type="check"] { background: var(--nc-accent-tint); border-color: transparent; }

/* "New" tags: mint outline pill. */
.nav-tag-pill { background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--nc-accent); color: var(--nc-accent); }

/* Code blocks: borders over shadows. */
.code-block, .code-group { border: 1px solid var(--nc-border); border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: none; }

12

Slides

Decks are 1920 × 1080 with 128px margins. The kit is in slides/ of the brand kit repo: deck.css (shared styles on these tokens), nine placeholder layouts, a PowerPoint template, and a preview of every layout. The full rules are in BRAND.md › Slides.

Three themes

Dark is the default. Light (class="light") is for dense data. Mint (class="mint") is for one statement slide per deck, at most, with near-black text and no wordmark.

Slide type scale

Hero 120 · Title 72 · Subtitle 48 · Quote 40 · Body 32 · Small 28 · Caption 24 (px, on the 1920 canvas; halve for points in PowerPoint). Nothing on a slide is under 24px. Split the slide instead.

Mint marks status

Big numbers stay in the text colour. Status is an icon and a word: check for success, clock or triangle for warning, triangle for risk. The “before” value in a comparison is muted grey.

The wordmark, not the lockup

28px tall, top right, on every slide but the cover and the mint slide. That's under 32px, so it's the wordmark alone. The cover gets the full lockup, at least 120px tall.

Code stays dark

Terminal output sits on the dark surface in JetBrains Mono on every theme. Show real output, trimmed. Never make it up.

Motion on arrival only

Elements rise or fade in, staggered by 100ms, with the whole slide shown within a second. No loops beside text, nothing that flashes.

Changelog

Unreleased

  • Slides (12): a slide kit in slides/, with dark, light and mint themes, a slide type scale (--nc-slide-*), nine layouts, a PowerPoint template and the rules for slides. Downloads and Changelog are now 13 and 14.

v1.3.1 · Nov 17, 2026

  • Wordmark only for small sizes. Under 32px tall, the logo drops the mascot and uses the wordmark alone (clear space = cap height, at least 64px wide); square spots keep the app icon. New files in avatar/logo/wordmark/, a Don’t for the squeezed lockup, and the footer now uses the wordmark.
  • Fix: on the light theme, the page’s inline mascot (hero, logo stages, sizes, Do/Don’t) had its mint body painted navy, because the wordmark’s colour switch also caught the mascot’s fill once both used #56EDD6. Only the wordmark switches colour now.
  • Top navigation fits every section without sideways scrolling: on wider screens the links get their own row.

v1.3 · Nov 17, 2026

  • One mint. The mascot’s fill, an almost identical and slightly greener mint, is now mint-400 #56EDD6, the wordmark’s and the UI’s mint, in every source and file. The shift is 7 units of blue (1.00:1), invisible side by side; now it is one value. The shading tones, #44BBAC and #89EDD6, are unchanged: they were picked from the drawn shading, not derived from the mint.
  • One near-black. #0C1213 is the brand near-black: the page, the reversed and mint variants, the variants sheet and the merch. Only previews of the README logos on GitHub use GitHub’s own #0d1117.
  • New sections: Voice and tone (07) and Downloads (12), with every master file and its path.
  • Light wordmark all navy. On light, the whole wordmark is navy #080037, the mascot’s outline colour; a teal “Claw” never matched the mascot’s mint. On dark: white “Nano”, mint “Claw”.
  • Logo variants (05): flat, two-colour spot, one colour (navy, black, reversed, mint), greyscale and outline, for the mascot, the lockup and the app icon.
  • Reversed and mint variants: a solid body, with the mascot’s own linework as a dark gap and an outer rim, in place of line art.
  • README logos use the 40% wordmark, the same artwork as the lockup.
  • Review fixes: the “Do” card text, the dark-stage caption contrast (3.5:1 → 7.6:1), no sideways scrolling on phones, the clear-space diagram drawn to scale, and the file paths.
